# Data-quality alert drill (P5)

A deliberate test that the P5 data-quality gate (`service/quality.mjs`) not only
*detects* an anomaly but *alerts* on one — because an alarm that has never fired is
not a proven alarm. Run on 2026-09-20.

**All data and load in this project are synthetic** (generated by `seed.mjs`, driven
by scheduled GitHub Actions). This drill induced a *simulated* data anomaly; no real
users, no organic traffic, and — see below — no actual mutation of the database.

## What was perturbed

Nothing in the database. The anomaly was simulated by temporarily changing one
baseline constant in `quality.mjs` (uncommitted, local only):

```
COUNTS.violation: 201619 -> 201618
```

so the checker expected one fewer `violation` row than the live table actually holds.
This exercises the exact same code path a real regression would (expected ≠ actual)
while keeping the database read-only — no `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, no transaction to roll
back, no risk to the seed data. The constant was restored immediately after.

## What fired

| Step | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Failed check, diagnostic output | `FAILED: 1 of 26 checks` → `Counts · violation: expected 201618, got 201619` |
| Non-zero exit | `exit=1` |
| Heartbeat **not** pinged | gate exits before the ping line, by design — the ping is reachable only after all 26 checks pass |
| Heartbeat went down | Better Stack heartbeat `495489` → 🔴 Down |
| Incident created + alert | incident `1018226775`, cause **"Missed heartbeat"**, started 08:59:18 UTC, email alert sent |

## Recovery

Restored the constant, re-ran the clean gate against the live DB:

```
all 26 checks passed.
heartbeat pinged: HTTP 200
```

Heartbeat `495489` returned to 🟢 Up and incident `1018226775` auto-resolved at
09:03:47 UTC — a ~4.5-minute incident, end to end.

## Note on timing

The production heartbeat's period is **1 day / 2 h grace** (it matches the daily
`quality.yml` cron). For this drill it was temporarily set to **3 min / 1 min** so a
withheld ping would trip the alarm in minutes rather than ~26 hours, then restored to
1 day / 2 h afterward. The alerting mechanism proven here is identical at either
period; only the timeout window differs.

## Why this matters

The gate's value is not that it passes — it's that when the live data diverges from
the deterministic baseline by even a single row, the log says *what* diverged and *by
how much* (`expected X, got Y`), and an operator is paged without anyone watching a
dashboard. This drill is the evidence that the whole chain works.
